A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we characterize incentive efficient equilibria of two-party sealed-bid bargaining games.
we have provided a set of sufficient and necessary conditions for the existence of an equilibrium that is interim efficient and ex postindividually-rational.
we have provided a set of sufficient conditions for a two-party bargaining game to have a strictly increasing equilibrium allocation that is interim incentive efficient.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in the absence of any information asymmetry between traders and when the trading environment is frictionless (i.e., when traders are not required to pay a fixed fee for the trading service), the only incentive efficient outcome is one that is also ex post individually rational.
a sealed-bid auction can be used to realize a bargaining outcome that is incentive efficient and ex post individually rational.
the equilibrium of a sealed bid mechanism can be incentive efficient, and that incentive efficiency is not necessarily lost by moving from a direct revelation mechanism to a sealed bid mechanism.
